CORE-001.note: Full linked ledger outcomes, authority, accessibility, privacy, persistence and all supported-platform acceptance remain Required.

CORE-002.note: Native display/desktop/runtime identity is XerahS/com.xerahs.app. Reference live settings are never imported implicitly. Previewed explicit replacement migration, backup and recovery remain Required.

CORE-003.note: Core conformance seams and stable native capture/activation errors exist. Shared result/error coverage, approved degraded modes and cross-platform parity remain Required.

CORE-004.note: Screenshot and editor loading have cancellation/failure tests. General progress, cancellation and recoverable terminal/output behavior across workflows, recording, uploads and all utilities remain Required.

CORE-005.note: Native portal consent and kernel-credential activation checks have isolated tests. Least-authority coverage for all sensitive operations and human security/privacy review remain Required.

CORE-006.note: Native launch uses a private runtime directory, lifetime flock and authenticated bounded local IPC. Real-process tests cover simultaneous launch, busy/rejection, crash recovery, corrupt/lost acknowledgements, unsafe paths and actual application forwarding before preference initialization. Default-profile production behavior is implemented; complete profile integration, target-matrix/security/compatibility review, published shared scenarios/vectors and accepted parity remain Required.

CORE-007.note: A native command window reuses actual tray actions and current capture availability, supports keyboard/accessible activation and preserves true capture results. Default repeated launch shows/restores the window. Region/Open activation shares the production dispatcher. Full main UI, workflow catalogue, global hotkeys, command palette, all surface availability and physical assistive-technology qualification remain Required.

CORE-008.note: Resumable accessible onboarding and explicit integration/permission/default-workflow choices remain Required.

CORE-009.note: Native editor preference and desktop appearance tests exist. Full application theming, localization, runtime expansion, high contrast and reduced-motion qualification remain Required.

CORE-010.note: Capture results reach the native tray and persist as plain accessible operation text in the command window. Full native policy, private-preview protection, result correlation and authority-limited actions remain Required.

CORE-011.note: Explicit/policy-scheduled signed update checks, channel/version display and install recovery remain Required.

CORE-012.note: An isolated private atomic editor preference store has recovery/unknown-field tests. All SETTINGS-CATALOG rows, shared profile/schema lifecycle and previewed import/migration/reset/export remain Required.

CORE-013.note: Approved Secret Service storage, references, revocation and diagnostic/interface redaction remain Required.

CORE-014.note: Native region snapshot intake exists. Full-screen/monitor/window target controls, per-monitor physical native sources, mixed scale, cursor/delay and all target/permission failure handling remain Required.

CORE-015.note: Scrolling capture selection, strategy, alignment/merge confidence, progress/cancellation/bounds/partial output remain Required.

CORE-016.note: Explicit bounded automatic capture schedules, target scope, visible stop/concurrency/lock/storage/privacy policy remain Required.

CORE-017.note: Video/GIF recording target, timing/codec/container/options and observable pause/stop/abort/recoverable failure states remain Required.

CORE-018.note: Selected system/microphone enumeration, consent, indication, mixing/synchronization and absent-device behavior remain Required.

CORE-019.note: Video editing and complete media utilities, formats/metadata/quality, progress/cancellation/temp-file/recovery behavior remain Required.

CORE-020.note: Native upload input/destination validation, credential references, progress/cancellation, bounded retry/idempotency and true publication outcomes remain Required.

CORE-022.note: Human-approved isolated plugin hosting, provenance/permissions/IPC/secrets/crash/revocation/audit remain Required.

CORE-023.note: Task/media history IDs, state/output references, search/pagination/retention/privacy/missing-file/corruption recovery remain Required. Editor recent paths do not implement task/media history.

CORE-024.note: The private native launch protocol has version/UUID correlation, kernel peer authentication, bounded intake/concurrency, redacted failures and limited receipt replay. This candidate is not an approved shared CLI/MCP API. Full shared operations, progress/cancellation, consent, assistant/shell/watch-folder coverage and human review remain Required.

CORE-025.note: Authorized canonical watch roots, readiness/duplicate/loop/traversal/checkpoint/failure/stop behavior remain Required.

CORE-026.note: Assistant provider/data flow minimization, explicit capture/history authority and sensitive/destructive review remain Required.

CORE-027.note: Native capture/activation publish stable value-free errors; activation failures have actionable text and unknown delivery never becomes success or a second instance. Full structured severity/correlation/retention/export/configuration/output recovery remain Required.

CORE-028.note: Desktop identity and dynamic Qt build exist. Signed/provenance-verified tar/deb/rpm/AUR packages, license obligations, clean install/replacement/update/rollback/uninstall qualification remain Required.

CORE-029.note: MOBILE-PLATFORM-001 declares Android/iOS scope; native mobile implementation is outside this Linux desktop target. Mobile and cross-platform acceptance gates remain open; no desktop requirement is waived.

CORE-030.note: Deterministic native/domain tests and six capabilities' published vectors run in baseline CI. CORE has no published test-vectors.json. All linked-row/platform acceptance and human security/privacy/accessibility/licensing/compatibility/parity reviews remain Required.

CORE-031.note: This CMake Linux edition introduces no NuGet dependency. Repository-wide authoritative NuGet maintenance before release qualification and the other contract triggers remain Required; no release qualification is claimed.

CORE-032.note: No NuGet adoption is part of this checkpoint. Complete repository-wide source/version/time/verification records and any bounded retention approvals remain Required before release qualification.

CORE-033.note: linux-qt is implemented as the supported reference candidate application. Every applicable requirement on every declared target remains Required; no scope reduction or edition promotion is claimed.

CORE-034.note: The approved linux-editions.json declares supported linux-qt and candidate editions. Actual qualification of all declared mechanisms and targets remains Required.

CORE-035.note: Desktop and runtime identity are shared com.xerahs.app. The current isolated native editor candidate store is edition-specific; approved shared persisted schemas/XDG formats, edition switching/replacement and explicit migration qualification remain Required.

CORE-036.note: Current published vectors run for linux-qt on Ubuntu baseline CI and the local toolchain. Every declared target distribution/native environment, accepted row disposition and complete shared conformance/parity remain Required.

CORE-037.note: Native Qt Widgets actions/keyboard/accessibility, portal capture and editor desktop appearance exist. Full convention/a11y/theming/notification/shortcut/configuration integration on GNOME/Plasma/wlroots remains Required. Candidate editions are not self-promoted.
